reasoning.text: The ISO render passes the X-ray test cleanly: the butterfly array is an open rail-and-floor frame with every copper multiplier, symmetric add/sub block and pipeline register exposed, the 8 interleaved BRAM banks read as distinct blue members along the -X edge, the Barrett reduction spine and the twiddle-ROM/addr-gen/PLL control cluster are all separately visible, and one representative radix-4 BU is exploded above with a labelled datapath and a fusion-callout strut. The only genuine wart was the exploded finned heatsink floating as a disconnected 'lollipop' at y=4 in the FRONT/SIDE elevations, far above everything else on an over-long stub; lowering it removes that read while keeping the exploded relationship legible. Structure is faithful to CFNTT — interleaved conflict-free banks + crossbar, 8 parallel radix-2/4 BUs, Barrett reduction, twiddle reuse ROM, address generator and a single wired FSM — with the invented PCIe/DMA boundary honestly flagged source-missing rather than presented as a paper claim. Every part carries real dimensions, a material, a concrete role and its verified spec; the connection graph is rooted at the PCB and reads as an assembly order.

fields.before: Exposed FPGA silicon die where the butterfly, K-RED multiplier and memory address logic are physically synthesized; the exploded overlay above is its floorplan lifted out on the four standoff risers.

fields.before: Shared 512-word twiddle ROM storing ONLY the 9^-1-scaled lower half of W (addresses 1..512); the psi-folded upper half (w_rom[512+j] = 7*w_rom[j] mod q) is NOT stored but reconstructed by the tf_fold7 gate on its output — was the largest block on the floorplan, now half the footprint.
fields.after: On-chip ROM storing precomputed roots of unity (psi^k / omega^k), reused across the rearranged loop so each factor is fetched once and broadcast over the feeder/rail to all eight multipliers.

params.word_stores: 9^-1-scaled lower half of W (9^-1 = 2731 mod q); addresses = w_rom[1..512]
params.psi: kesai = 7; upper half w_rom[512+j] = 7*w_rom[j] mod q
params.replaces: tf_ROM.v (1023 words) with tf_rom_fold.v, same interface, 1-cycle latency

before.notes: v2 psi-fold: only the lower half is stored; the upper half derives via tf_fold7. Measured 7828 -> 1611 cells (-79%), stored bits 14322 -> 7168 (-50%). Formally verified equivalent to the shipped tf_ROM.v at every address (SymbiYosys miter, 9*Q_new == Q_ref mod q).

params.primitive_root_psi: psi = g^6 = 11^6 mod 12289 = 1945 (order 2048; psi^1024 ≡ -1 mod 12289, i.e. negacyclic)
params.j_fourth_root: j = psi^512 (order 4, j^2 ≡ -1 ≡ 12288 mod q); used as the constant rotator by the radix-4 butterflies
params.psi_inv: psi^{-1} mod q via Fermat (psi^{q-2}); INTT uses psi^{-i}/omega^{-k} twiddles together with N^-1 = 12277
params.psi_power_table_sample: entry[k] = psi^k mod 12289 with psi=1945: psi^0=1, psi^1=1945, psi^2=10302(=omega), psi^3=6320, psi^4=3400, ...; structural anchors psi^512=j (j^2≡12288≡-1), psi^1024≡12288≡-1 (negacyclic sign flip), psi^2048≡1; the omega table is the even subsequence omega^k = psi^(2k). The full 0..2047 table is generated by iterated multiply-by-1945-mod-12289 from this seed (bit-exact, no bit-reversal indexing).
params.stored: omega^k stage twiddles for k=0..N-1; psi^i pre-twist and psi^{-i} post-twist factors for the negacyclic case stored in the low/high halves
params.addressing: address = f(stage s, butterfly-block index); one fetch reused across all 8 lanes per block
params.table_contents: entry[s][block] = omega raised to the block's stage exponent (no bit-reversal indexing); negacyclic twist factors keyed by coefficient index i

after.notes:
Depth N=1024 covers every stage twiddle without bit-reversal. Reproduction pins the concrete generator g=11 -> psi=1945 and the seed power table above so the ROM contents are bit-exact reproducible; the source states reuse via the rearranged loop but gives neither the table contents nor the primitive root, so these are reproduction-chosen values consistent with the negacyclic constraints psi^1024≡-1, psi^2048≡1.
[conv] CT/DIT merged-negacyclic layout (Longa-Naehrig style): single ROM of N=1024 entries holding psi^(brv(k)) so stage s reads the 2^s twiddles at base 2^s sequentially; INTT uses the inverse table. [src] psi=1945. [calc] entries are powers of 1945 mod 12289. [source-missing] the paper's exact f(stage,block) addressing under its rearranged loop (which reuses twiddles across the loop) may index differently; the standard CT addressing above is the committed reproducible choice (only a seed table was implied). RESIDUAL TENSION: this committed bit-reversed ROM layout coexists with the paper's claimed natural-order/no-bit-reversal datapath — the bit-reversal lives only in the ROM index, not the coefficient stream, but the paper's rearranged-loop addressing that avoids even that is not transcribed.
Seed twiddle table = powers of psi=1945 mod 12289 [calc], depth 1024. Committed the standard 2^stage+block bit-reversed address that both impls assumed [conv]. The paper's actual twiddle-ROM addressing f(stage,block) under the rearranged-loop twiddle-reuse structure (loop-restructure + factor reuse to drop bit-reversal) is [source-missing] [paper] — mechanism confirmed by abstract, explicit formula not extractable.
Stores psi-powers (negacyclic). psi=1945=11^6 mod 12289 (order 2048), omega=psi^2=10302, ninv=1024^-1=12277 [src][calc]. Paper avoids bit-reversal by 'rearranging the loop structure and reusing twiddle factors' [paper]; the explicit rearranged addressing f(stage,block) is [source-missing] — impls fell back to a bit-reversed ROM, which contradicts the no-bit-reversal claim, so f(stage,block) must come from the paper body.
Address function pins the higher-confidence Impl-2 form as [conv]. psi=1945=11^6 mod 12289, omega=10302=psi^2 mod 12289 [calc]. [source-missing] the paper's rearranged-loop reuse addressing that achieves natural-order (no bit-reversal) output — current ROM still embeds bit-reversal, so the headline no-bit-reversal property is not yet met.
Stores psi powers (negacyclic twist) [src]. Reuse-via-rearranged-loop mechanism confirmed [paper:abstract]; explicit f(stage,block) addressing formula [source-missing] — committed (1<<stage)+block placeholder [conv].
ops: sequential bit-reversed psi-power lookup per CT/DIT stage
broadcast one twiddle to the 8 BU lanes (twiddle reuse)
addr(stage, j) = bitrev10(2^stage + j) [conv standard bit-reversed layout]
addr = f(stage,block) under rearranged twiddle-reuse loop [paper-mechanism; explicit formula source-missing]

fields.before: Machined cold plate spreading heat off the die into the finned stack above; footprint kept inside the standoff ring so the risers clear it.
fields.after: EXPLODED ABOVE: the aluminum finned heatsink (the package thermal lid) that clamps onto the FPGA package over the +X control/reduction region of the die, lifted on a riser stub so it floats clearly above the datapath and the Barrett reduction spine. Lowered this pass (y=3.4, riser 2.6 m) so it no longer reads as disconnected debris high in the FRONT/SIDE elevations while staying unmistakably exploded above the control cluster. Its footprint was shrunk (z-extent -1.3..1.3) so the twiddle ROM (z=-2.5), address-generation (z=+2.5) and schedule blocks below stay visible in the ISO X-ray and the TOP plan view rather than being swallowed. Eight 0.12 m fins at 0.3 m pitch over a 2.4x2.6 m baseplate, modeled as ONE finned block (the fin comb is decoration captured in spec, not eight separate parts).

after.notes: Consolidated finned heatsink — the prior ten heatsink_fin_* parts were pure decoration and were collapsed into this single block with the fin geometry recorded in params (anti-decoration rule). Footprint reduced and, this pass, lowered (y 4.0->3.4, riser 3.5->2.6 m) so it no longer blankets the +X control cluster in plan view nor floats as disconnected debris in the elevations; it represents the exploded package thermal lid, not full-die coverage.

meta.before: Root everything on the PCB. Populate the board: a gold PCIe edge connector, the FPGA BGA package carrying the exposed silicon die, an in-package HBM stack on each side, a clock oscillator, two bulk decoupling caps and an auxiliary power tap; a brushed-steel cold plate and its finned stack cap the die. From the four die corners, four thin brushed-steel standoff risers (clear of the heatsink footprint) lift an exploded logic-floorplan plate directly above the die; the plate carries the synthesized CFNTT-KRED butterfly datapath (compact_bf_v2). Two conflict-free memory banks (white composite) with their address generators stream u/v coefficients into input DFFs. A single shared half-size 512-word twiddle ROM (black composite) stores only the 9^-1-scaled lower half of W; its output passes through a small copper fold7 derive-gate (x<<3 minus x, then three conditional subtractions, zero multipliers) that reconstructs the psi-folded upper half, then feeds the w delay chain — so the biggest block on the floorplan is halved and two tiny copper derive-gates replace the missing half. Before the multiplier two selects sit: v_mux picks the A operand (v for NTT, v-u for INTT) and the NTT/INTT mux picks the B operand (W or op21(W)). The K-RED modular multiplier is a 4-stage pipeline — ONE 14x14->28 hardware multiplier (brass), then two shift-add fold stages (d = 3z+6q-z>>12; e = 3d+q-d>>12) and one conditional subtraction — producing 9*A*B mod q. A modular_add combines u with the product; two modular_half (op21) copper gates, one on the ROM output side and one on the add path, derive the per-stage INTT halving that fixes the reference's 2^10-scaling bug, with add_mux selecting the halved sum onto the bank writeback during INTT. A copper PWM return bus feeds the K-RED result back into v_mux for the double-pass mode. A control FSM sequences the banks, ROM addresses, both muxes and the sel line; a copper datapath bus threads the stages.
meta.after: 1) Start from the FPGA PCB substrate (14x9 m floorplan) and overlay the silicon-die outline plate that bounds the placed-and-routed logic, then scribe three thin floorplan partition lines dividing the die into memory, butterfly-array and reduction/control zones; on the -X edge seat the host interface: a PCIe x16 gold-finger edge connector feeding a host DMA/PCIe controller block, the boundary where coefficient vectors enter and transformed results leave. 2) Drive the controller into the forward-NTT input FIFO and natural-order output FIFO, then mount the eight interleaved BRAM banks along the left edge at 1.1 m pitch between them. 3) Drop the conflict-free crossbar network as a vertical spine just inboard of the banks, and place the inverse-NTT N^-1 scaling unit on its output side. 4) Build the open butterfly-array frame: lay a thin floor across the array, then bolt the two longitudinal steel rails and the mid cross-brace so the chassis stays open from above; populate the eight parallel radix-2 butterfly lanes (one per BRAM bank) by wiring each DSP modular multiplier into its symmetric modular adder (dark anodized) and subtractor (brushed steel), then both into the pipeline register; finally seat the four carbon-fiber radix-4 fusion yokes in the open gap between the multiplier and add/sub columns, each binding a lane-pair (0-1, 2-3, 4-5, 6-7) into one fused 4-input radix-4 butterfly unit so the eight radix-2 lanes reconfigure into four radix-4 BUs. 5) Place the shared modular-reduction stage to the right as two distinct members, lifted slightly so they read above the pipeline-register column: first the cylindrical Barrett q-multiplier spanning all eight lanes, then the boxy shift/subtract+correction member abutting it, wired from every pipeline register. 6) Route the operand-return bus from the reduction member back over the array to the crossbar (grounded by a standoff post onto the reduction member), and route the operand-read bus from the crossbar east into the multiplier column (grounded by its own standoff onto the array frame), keeping the read, return and twiddle channels on three separate heights; cap each with a direction arrow so the read/twiddle/return dataflow triad is fully visible and the conflict-free read-modify-write loop is closed. 7) On the right, install the twiddle-factor ROM and route a brass broadcast feeder west to the elevated rail spanning the multiplier column (grounded by a standoff onto the array frame) so one fetched factor fans out to all eight multipliers; then add the address-generation unit, the radix-2/4 config selector, the schedule/FSM controller and the clock PLL. 8) For inspection, lift one fused radix-4 butterfly unit onto two riser posts into an exploded view above the array (three twiddle multipliers W1/W2/W3 -> constant j-rotator -> y0..y3 add/sub tree -> four-output register), offset toward the +Z half so it clears the central lanes in plan view; add two +X dataflow arrows (mult->add/sub, add/sub->register) on the exploded unit and a thin carbon-fiber fusion-callout strut from the lanes-6/7 yoke up to the exploded baseplate so the W1->W2->W3->j-rotator->add/sub->register order and the represented fused unit are unambiguous, and clamp the finned aluminum heatsink (the exploded package thermal lid) on its riser stub above the +X control region, sized so the twiddle ROM, address-generation and schedule blocks below stay visible in plan.
